description: Published transit validation of other travel models, for comparison with this model's route-level fit (Muni routes) and rail-station fit (BART). For each model: what was compared with what, base year, model structure, whether the comparison was fitted, and the route- and station-level statistics as published or as computed here from a published table of observed and modeled values. The article (client/beta3/paper/sections/front.ts, validation.ts, closing.ts) reads the 'comparison' rows and 'tm1Table74'.
rule: Every number was read from the cited document as fetched. Statistics marked computed: true were computed here (FHWA definitions: %RMSE = 100*sqrt(mean((M-O)^2))/mean(O); r = Pearson correlation of modeled and observed; within25 = share of routes with |M/O-1| <= 0.25) from the observed and modeled values printed in the source table; the transcribed tables were checked against the source totals and, where printed, against each row's ratio. Statistics without that flag are as published. Nothing is estimated from charts except where marked uncertain.
rawDir: data/beta3/raw/benchmarks/ (gitignored); TM1 2011, TM1.5.2, TM1.6.1, TAMDM, and the standards documents are in data/beta3/raw/standards/
whatDiffers: Observed data: this model is compared with SFMTA automatic passenger counts (twelve-month mean of weekdays, 2025-26). TM1 2005 and SF-CHAMP 3 used year-2000 counts or a Muni on-board survey; TM1 2010 used operator counts scaled with NTD; ARC and the Met Council used expanded on-board surveys; LA Metro and SANDAG used automatic passenger counts. Survey-expanded route totals carry sampling and expansion error.
Base years range from 2000 (SF-CHAMP 3) to 2022 (SANDAG ABM3); this model's is 2025-26. Muni's network and ridership differ greatly between those years.

Fitted or not: this model's Muni total and Metro/bus ratio are calibrated and its route counts were examined during development (a development set, not an independent test). SF-CHAMP 3 and TM1 matched Muni totals by mode within a few percent but did not fit routes. SANDAG, ARC, PSRC, and the Met Council calibrated mode choice or networks to the same transit data they report. LA Metro calibrated to 2012 and compared with 2017 counts after network fixes. STOPS's national results are before its local count adjustment.

Statistic: several agencies publish only R-squared of a fitted line (PSRC, SANDAG, ARC, TM1 2010). R-squared is dominated by the largest routes and can be high while the %RMSE is large (Met Council: R-squared 0.97, %RMSE 45%).
Scope: the agency models are regional (TM1, TM2, SANDAG, ARC, PSRC, CMAP, MWCOG) or city models with regional demand (SF-CHAMP); this model covers San Francisco and trips with one end in it.
Period: most comparisons are daily weekday boardings; PSRC's route statistic is for the AM peak.
